page.layout: One page of running text in one column, with a short italic note in the right margin beside the first line. Running head at top centre. Page number at top left. Below the text: gathering signature "P 4" and catchword "remis-" at the right.

main_text.p: In Applica-tioneQuoad applicationem, multis modis commendatur gratia & benignitas Dei. Deus enim proponit filium suum placamentum in sanguine ejus. Rom.3.25. Ante faciem omnium populorum, Luc.2.32[?] instituens & confervans minifterium reconciliationis, 2.Corint.5.18. Et Deus omnis gratiæ vocat nos ad suam gloriam, 1.Pet.5.10. Gal.1.2[?] Vocavit & me per suam gratiam. Rom.8.28. Qui secundum propositum vocati sumus sancti. 2.Tim.1.9. Qui nos liberavit, & vocavit vocatione sancta, non secundum opera nostra, sed secundum suum propositum & gratiam. Col.1.12. Idoneos nos reddit ad participationem sortis sanctorum, dando resipiscentiam. Act.5.31. Dando fidem. 1.Tim.1.14. Superabundavit misericordia in fide, 2.Thess.2.16. Dilexit nos & dedit consolationem & Spem bonam in gratia, &c. Ephes.2.v.4. &c. Deus igitur, qui dives est in Misericordia, propter nimiam suam caritatem, qua dilexit nos, cum mortui essemus in peccatis, convivificavit nos cum Christo. Unde Ephes.1.7. habemus remis-

page.notes: The number "334" at the top right corner is outside the printed page block and looks like a scan or library number, so it is left out. The page number "212" is hard to read: the first digit may be "2" or "I" and is marked [?]. The margin note "In Applica-tione" is set in italic and split across two lines with a mark; the hyphenation is reconstructed. Doubtful Scripture references are marked [?]: "Luc.2.32" and "Gal.1.2". The reference "Ephes.2.v.4." is copied as printed, with the odd "v." left in place. The long s in "Ephes", "Thess" and "remis-" is written as plain s.
